chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you are in the seventh circumambulation, go to the Mu'tawwadh (place of refuge), which is when you stand behind the Ka'bah opposite the door, and say: O God, the House is Your House, and the servant is Your servant, and this is the standing place of the one seeking refuge in You from the Fire. O God, from You comes relief and deliverance. Then touch the Yemeni Corner, then go to the Hajar (stone) and conclude with it.'

key_terms.الْمُتَعَوَّذَ: the place of refuge (behind the Ka'bah)
key_terms.مَقَامُ الْعَائِذِ: the standing place of the one seeking refuge

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication and ritual action at the Mu'tawwadh during the seventh Tawaf?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the spiritual significance of the seventh Tawaf, emphasizing the 'Mu'tawwadh' (place of refuge) as a locus for seeking divine pardon. The supplication underscores the theological concept of *al-Bayt* (the House) as God’s own domain, inviting the pilgrim to transition from servitude to intimate reliance on Allah’s mercy before concluding with the tactile connection to the Yemeni Corner and the Hajar al-Aswad.
